evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: ~11.2 mg/L at 50.0 h collapsing to ~4.5-5.3 mg/L from 50.2-52.0 h
Receiving delayed P assays: 0 g/L @12h, 0.014 @24h, 1.077 @36h, 3.010 g/L @48h (sampled t=48, available 52.0h)
Source batches (1-3) at same 48-52 h window maintained DO2 ~10.6-11.2 mg/L; P @48h 2.98-3.06 g/L — receiving oxygen behavior diverges despite comparable production
Forward model KEEP: min DO 1.46 mg/L, below-limit 4.6 h, infeasible; increase_air: 1.65 mg/L, 2.8 h, infeasible; combined: 1.82 mg/L, 1.2 h, infeasible
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.96 mg/L, 0 h below limit, product mass 272.6 kg, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
args.rationale: At the decision time (52 h), receiving DO2 has abruptly collapsed from ~11 mg/L to ~4.5-5.3 mg/L within 2 hours and is still trending down, while product is in active production (P=3.01 g/L at 48 h, matching source batches that kept DO2 near 9-11 mg/L). This is an oxygen-demand/receipt-capacity mismatch emerging at ~50 h. The nominal source-calibrated forward model predicts KEEP, increase_air, and combined all violate the 2.0 mg/L DO limit (minimum DO 1.46, 1.65, 1.82 mg/L respectively), while strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) keeps minimum DO at ~2.96 mg/L with zero below-limit hours and is the only action with feasible majority (4/5) in sensitivity analysis. Counterintuitively it also yields the highest predicted product mass (272.6 kg vs 206-243 kg for others), because avoiding oxygen deficit preserves continued production; a stop would count zero production. Stop is rejected outright. Weaker interventions were evaluated and rejected because they leave the batch predicted oxygen-infeasible, risking a forced stop later.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; receiving transfer multiplier is estimated (0.54), and sensitivity members still show min-DO range 1.42-3.74 mg/L, so one of five members violates the limit even under this action. The DO2 collapse cause is inferred (demand exceeding receipt), not directly measured; if the drop were a sensor or aeration-equipment fault rather than metabolic demand, feed reduction would sacrifice productivity unnecessarily. No off-cycle assay was requested because product assays have 4 h turnaround and the urgent constraint is DO2, which is continuously monitored.
